questions.question: On a number line, you start at 48 and jump forward 37. What number do you land on?
questions.explain: Round 48 up to 50. Now 50 + 37 = 87. You went 2 too far, so take 2 back to get 85. The trap is stopping at 87 and forgetting to fix it.

questions.question: On a number line, you start at 200 and jump back 58. Where do you land?
questions.explain: Round 58 up to 60. Now 200 - 60 = 140. You went 2 too far, so add 2 back to get 142. Stopping at 140 or sliding the wrong way to 138 are the common slips.

questions.question: On a number line, start at 350 and jump forward 198. What number is that?
questions.explain: Round 198 up to 200. Now 350 + 200 = 550. You added 2 too many, so take 2 back to get 548. Forgetting that last step gives 550.

questions.question: On a number line, start at 400 and jump back 197. Where do you land?
questions.explain: Round 197 up to 200. Now 400 - 200 = 200. You jumped 3 too far, so add 3 back to get 203. Stopping at 200 is the most common slip.

questions.question: Mia has 243 stickers. Her friend gives her 199 more. How many stickers does Mia have now?
questions.explain: Round 199 up to 200. Now 243 + 200 = 443. You added 1 too many, so take 1 back to get 442. Forgetting to take that 1 back gives 443.

questions.question: A bus has 350 seats. 187 seats are taken. How many seats are empty?
questions.explain: Round 187 up to 190. Now 350 - 190 = 160. You subtracted 3 too many, so add 3 back to get 163. Stopping at 160 forgets the fix.

questions.question: Sam wants to do 625 + 199 in his head. He rounds 199 to 200 first. What should he do next?
questions.explain: Since 200 is 1 more than 199, you must take 1 away after adding. Adding 1 back or just stopping are the two most common slips.

questions.question: A jar holds 500 marbles. Lena pours out 198. How many marbles are still in the jar?
questions.explain: Round 198 up to 200. Now 500 - 200 = 300. You took 2 too many, so add 2 back to get 302. Forgetting to add those 2 back gives 300.

questions.question: Owen has 450 stamps. He gives 98 to his sister, then buys 97 more at a fair. How many does he have now?
questions.explain: First 450 - 98: round 98 to 100, get 350, add 2 back to get 352. Then 352 + 97: round 97 to 100, get 452, take 3 back to get 449. Forgetting either fix gives a wrong total.

questions.question: 725 minus a missing number equals 529. What is the missing number?
questions.explain: Work backwards: 725 - 529. Round 529 to 530, get 725 - 530 = 195, add 1 back to get 196. Forgetting that add-back gives 195.

questions.question: At a bake sale, 348 cookies are baked. In the morning, 149 are sold. In the afternoon, 97 more are sold. How many are left?
questions.explain: 348 - 149: round 149 to 150, get 198, add 1 back to get 199. Then 199 - 97: round 97 to 100, get 99, add 3 back to get 102. Missing either fix gives 101 or 99.

questions.question: Alex works out 512 + 199. He says: 512 + 200 = 712, so the answer is 712. What went wrong?
options: He added 1 instead of taking 1 away
He rounded 199 to 200, which is wrong
He forgot to take 1 away from 712
questions.explain: Rounding 199 to 200 is fine, but 200 is 1 more than 199, so he must take 1 away from 712 to get 711. Forgetting that step is the most common slip with compensating.
